info.description:
Backend API for the AIFU Learning Platform.

**Authentication** — `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns a short-lived
JWT access token (15 min) plus an opaque refresh token (30 days,
single use, rotated). Send the access token as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**Errors** — every failure returns the `ApiError` envelope with a
stable `code` your client may branch on, plus a `requestId` to quote
in bug reports.

**Localization** — content endpoints accept `?locale=uz|ru|en` and
report `resolvedLocale` / `availableLocales` / `fallback` so the UI can
flag untranslated content.

**Async execution** — `POST /api/v1/submissions` (graded) and
`POST /api/v1/runs` (not graded) only queue the work; poll
`GET /api/v1/submissions/{id}` or `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}` until
`status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`.

**Pagination** — list endpoints take `page` (from 0), `size` and
`sort=property,asc|desc`, and answer a `PageResponse…` envelope.

post.description:
Exchanges credentials for an access token and a refresh token.

The access token is a short-lived JWT to be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
The refresh token is an opaque, single-use value: calling `/auth/refresh` consumes it
and returns a new pair. Presenting an already-consumed refresh token revokes the whole
token family, on the assumption that it leaked.

Failures always return `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` with HTTP 401, whether the account
is unknown, the password is wrong, or the account is locked. Check the audit log for
the real reason.
post.summary: Log in

post.description: Revokes the supplied refresh token. Idempotent by design: an unknown or already revoked token still returns 204, so a client can always safely clear state.

post.description: Revokes every refresh token for the caller. Use after a suspected compromise.
